title: How to Get More Leads for a Painting Business
description: Painting business leads that are yours, not shared: Google profile, reviews, job-site signs, referrals, and paid lead costs for 2026.

cover.alt: Illustration of a megaphone on a for pros blueprint background with a measuring tape

takeaways: Your Google Business Profile and review count bring the cheapest steady leads a painter can get. Both are free to build.
Shared leads from marketplaces often cost $40 to $80 each and go to several painters at once. Owned channels close far more often.
Speed wins the job. Reply within minutes when you can, then follow up on days 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30.
body:
Painting leads come from four places, in this order: your Google Business Profile, your own website, the blocks you are already painting on, and past customers who send friends your way. Paid ads fill gaps when you need work fast. Build the free channels first, because a lead you own costs you time once, while a bought lead costs you cash every single time and is often sold to three to five painters at once.

## Channel 1: your Google profile and reviews

When a homeowner searches for a painter near them, the map results and the reviews beside your name do most of the selling. Claim your profile, fill every field, set your true service area, and add clear before and after photos of real jobs. Twenty or more project photos is a good working target. Then ask every finished customer for a review, the same day, with your direct link.

Reviews do double duty. They push your profile up the local results, and they answer the trust question before you ever get a call. A painter with 60 recent reviews and a 4.8 rating gets called over a painter with 6 reviews, even at a higher price. Our full system for this is in [how to get more Google reviews](/blog/get-more-google-reviews/), and the setup steps are in our [Google Business Profile guide for contractors](/blog/google-business-profile-for-contractors/). Price pages help too: a page that answers what a room costs, like our guide to the [cost to paint a room](/blog/cost-to-paint-a-room/), brings searchers who are ready to hire, not just browsing colors.

## Worked example: what $500 of paid leads really buys

Use Local Services Ads figures reported for painting in 2026: about $33 a lead in the 99 Calls campaign data. This is a planning example. Run it with your own close rate after a month.

- Budget: $500
- Cost per lead: about $33
- Leads bought: $500 / $33 = about 15 leads
- If you close 1 in 3, jobs won: 15 / 3 = 5 jobs
- Cost per closed job: $500 / 5 = $100
- At an example job value of $3,500: 5 x $3,500 = $17,500 of work from $500 of ads

Check it backward: $17,500 of work, at $3,500 a job, is 5 jobs. Five jobs from 15 leads is a 33 percent close rate, and $500 over 5 jobs is $100 per job. The math holds, but only if your close rate holds. Now compare a shared marketplace lead at $60, a price FieldCamp reports for HomeAdvisor-type leads: $500 / $60 = about 8 leads, and those 8 leads also went to other painters. If your close rate on shared leads drops to 1 in 5, you win 1 to 2 jobs, and your cost per job jumps to $250 to $500. Same budget, very different month. That is why owned channels come first and paid leads fill gaps, not the other way round. Price each won job with our [painting estimate calculator](/blog/painting-estimate-calculator/) so a cheap lead never turns into a cheap job.

## Channel 2: the block you are already on

Every job site is a small billboard in the exact streets you want to work. Put a yard sign in the front yard with the owner permission, from setup day to cleanup day. While the crew is visibly working, knock the six closest doors or drop hangers on the two nearest blocks. The proof of your work is right there on the wall, which is why this converts better than any cold ad. PaintViz reports painters commonly see 1 to 3 estimate requests per job from the sign and hangers around one finished house.

Make the sign and hangers earn the tap: your business name, one line on what you paint, a phone number in big type, and a QR code to your quote form or review page. Take a before photo on day one and an after photo from the same spot. That pair goes on your profile, your site and your social pages the same week, with the owner permission.

## Channel 3: referrals and trade partners

Past customers close at the highest rate of any channel, often 60 to 80 percent in PaintViz reporting, because trust arrives before you do. Ask at the final walk, when the room is done and the client is smiling: "Who do you know who has been talking about painting?" Then stay in touch twice a year with a short note or a seasonal tip, so your name is the one they remember in month nine.

Build the same habit with people who see houses before you do: real estate agents, property managers, flooring and drywall crews, and the counter staff at your paint store. Give each of them your card, your typical turnaround and one clear way to reach you fast. Send work back when you can.

## Paid options, with honest 2026 costs

| Channel | Typical cost | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google Business Profile and reviews | Free, your time | Ask every customer, or the flow stops |
| Yard signs and door hangers | Under $1 a piece in bulk | Needs owner permission and a QR code that works |
| Local Services Ads for painters | About $33 a lead (99 Calls 2026 data) | Pay per lead, dispute bad leads fast |
| Shared marketplace leads | About $40 to $80 a lead | Same lead sold to 3 to 5 painters |
| Google Search Ads for painters | Median about $157 to $193 a lead in early 2026 (99 Calls) | Needs a tight service area and a page that answers price |

Start paid spend small and judge it on cost per closed job, not cost per lead. A $33 lead you close 1 time in 3 costs you $100 a job. A $20 lead you close 1 time in 10 costs you $200 a job. Track the source of every lead on a simple sheet: date, name, channel, quoted or not, won or lost, job value. After 20 to 30 leads, your own numbers beat any article, including this one.

## Your first week checklist

- Claim and complete your Google Business Profile, with service area and 20-plus job photos
- Set up your review link and add the ask to your final walk
- Order yard signs and door hangers with a QR code to your quote form
- Make one price page on your site that answers a real cost question
- List 10 past customers and 5 trade partners, and contact each one this week
- Start a lead tracking sheet and log every inquiry from today on
- Reply to every new lead within minutes when you can, and set follow-ups for days 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30

Slow follow-up is the silent leak in most painting businesses. A homeowner who gets three quotes usually hires the painter who answered first and sounded ready. If a lead goes quiet, the day 3, 7 and 14 touches bring back jobs a single call would have lost. Keep each touch short: hold their date, offer a measure time, or send a photo of a similar job. Our [contractor website checklist](/blog/contractor-website-checklist/) covers the site basics that turn these visits into quote requests.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the cheapest way to get painting leads?
Your Google Business Profile, your reviews and the block you are working on. All three are free apart from your time and a few dollars of signs and hangers, and painters report 1 to 3 estimate requests per finished job from job-site signs and hangers alone.

### How much do painting leads cost in 2026?
Local Services Ads leads for painters ran about $33 each in 2026 campaign data from 99 Calls. Shared marketplace leads often run $40 to $80 each and go to several painters. Google Search Ads leads for painters had a median near $157 to $193 each in the first months of 2026 in the same firm data.

### Are shared lead services worth it for painters?
As a starter while your own channels grow, maybe. As your main source, no. You pay for each lead, share it with 3 to 5 competitors and close at a lower rate, so your cost per closed job can reach $250 to $500 on the worked example above.

### How fast should I reply to a new painting lead?
Within minutes if you can, and the same day at the latest. Homeowners often book the first painter who answers and offers a measure time. Then follow up on days 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 before you close the file.

### How many reviews do I need to compete locally?
There is no fixed number. Compare the top three painters in your service area on Google Maps: their review counts are your working target. Getting to 50 or more recent reviews, with replies to each one, puts most small painters in a strong local spot.

## Next step
Pick the free channels first this week: finish your profile, start the review ask and put a sign on your current job.
